value.strategy: The investment process combines several strategies: a long/short directional strategy to optimize performance based on interest rate and inflation expectations; an interest rate curve strategy to exploit variations in spreads between long-term and short-term rates; an arbitrage strategy to seek relative value across various bond asset classes; and a credit strategy focused on private sector bonds. The Sub-Fund's modified duration will range between -3 and +7. It also integrates responsible and sustainable principles. The Sub-Fund will invest no more than 25% of its total assets in bonds from non-OECD issuers. It mainly invests in fixed rate, floating rate, or inflation-indexed debt securities and negotiable debt. Convertible or exchangeable bonds can be up to 100% of total assets, and Contingent Convertible Bonds (CoCo Bonds) at most 20%. Equity market exposure, resulting from convertible bonds and derivatives, is limited to 10% of total assets. Non-base currency exposure may be hedged.
value.philosophy: The Sub-Fund is managed taking into consideration responsible and sustainable principles, promoting environmental and/or social characteristics within the meaning of Article 8 of SFDR. This involves an extra-financial analysis through a proprietary rating model (ABA, Above & Beyond Analysis) developed internally, centered on corporate responsibility, controversies, and dialogue/engagement with issuers. The analysis of corporate responsibility is broken down into four aspects: shareholders, environmental, workers, and society responsibility, each rated independently and weighted.
value.selection_process: The initial investment universe comprises Government bonds from United Nation countries (integrating SDGs), corporate bonds and related securities from OECD countries (minimum B- rating by S&P or equivalent), and supranational agencies. Issuers with controversies or in severe breach of UN Global Compact Principles are excluded, along with a strict controversial weapons and sectorial exclusion policy. The investment process incorporates internal scoring based on extra-financial analysis via the proprietary ABA model. For public issuers, ESG matters (Environment, Social, Governance), ESG risks analysis (Governance, Environment, Social, Society pillars), international standards infraction, international convention engagement, and climate profile are considered. Extra-financial analysis is performed on at least 90% of securities (excluding cash, cash equivalents, derivatives, and money market funds), with 20% of the worst issuers (high-risk profile in corporate responsibility or country score below 2/10 in the ESG tool) being excluded. Securities must have a rating of at least B- by Standard & Poor's or equivalent at purchase. If unrated, the issue level must meet this condition. Downgraded bonds (below B-) are not necessarily sold but cannot exceed 10% of total assets. Analysis relies on factual data and continuous dialogue with company managers.
value.asset_types: Government bonds (from UN countries), corporate bonds and related securities (from OECD countries), supranational agencies bonds, fixed rate, floating rate or inflation-indexed debt securities, negotiable debt, convertible or exchangeable bonds, contingent convertible bonds (Coco Bonds), listed derivative instruments on equity or equity indices, and UCITS or regulated AIFs (up to 10% of net assets). Securities can be denominated in any currency.
value.real_objectives: To optimize the performance of the portfolio based on interest rate and inflation expectations, exploit variations of spreads between long-term and short-term rates, seek relative value on various bond asset classes, and promote environmental and/or social characteristics (Article 8 SFDR).
